A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, framework, applications and core proofs. All 22 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original battery-storage and synthetic portfolio experiments, including task loss and coverage across ten runs in Figures 2–7.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for both applications and adds tail-risk evaluations, runtime measurements and case analyses in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The training algorithm, exact-quantile differentiation and PICNN construction remain. However, the printed box score changes from maximum signed residuals in v1 Section 3.2 to maximum infinity norms in v2 Section 3.1. These are not equivalent, although the claimed interval remains unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether this formula change reached the implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 2011–2016 PJM battery dataset and Gaussian-mixture portfolio dataset. Random and chronological battery test scenarios already appear in v1. The new geometric illustration and case visualizations do not establish additional empirical dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: ETO, ETO-SLL and ETO-JC retain their corresponding uncertainty-set comparisons. However, v2 Table A2 omits the perfect-information 'optimal' reference included in v1's portfolio Figure 6, while retaining that reference in the battery comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 changes the reported portfolio PICNN width from 128 to 32 after testing 32/64/128 units, and replaces the E2E learning-rate search over 10^-3 and 10^-4 with 5×10^-3. The PICNN ETO tuning grid also changes. VaR/CVaR metrics and runtime measurements extend evaluation within the retained tasks and splits.

E4.justification: v2 adds battery tail-risk analyses under both existing distribution conditions (Figures A1–A2), runtime profiling (Table A1), a portfolio uncertainty-set and decision case study (Figure A3), and detailed characterization of the temporal distribution shift (Figure A4). These substantially extend the questions examined beyond v1's average-loss and coverage comparisons.

E5.justification: Predictive-performance results retain mean ± one standard deviation across ten runs. v2 additionally specifies timing variability across ten epochs in Table A1 and descriptive standard-deviation bands for electricity-price data in Figure A4. No increase in experimental run counts or new significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: Reported battery results change: at alpha=0.01 without shift, E2E ellipse task loss is approximately -37.8 in v1 Figure 2 versus -26.5 in v2 Figure 3. Portfolio results are also revised, alongside changed PICNN settings. v2 adds extensive VaR/CVaR results, runtime values and case-specific losses, rather than merely redisplaying existing results.

T1.justification: v2 generalizes the loss assumption from yᵀFz to yᵀF(x,z), with F affine in z, and updates the corresponding formulations. It corrects the stated finite-sample quantile level and specifies probability 'at least' 1-alpha for the loss bound. Core appendix proofs remain; the non-equivalent box-score rewrite introduces an inconsistency with its stated uncertainty set.

C1.justification: v2 qualifies the introductory PICNN approximation claim as covering arbitrary compact convex uncertainty sets, whereas v1 says arbitrary convex sets. The central contributions—end-to-end conformal calibration, expressive PICNN uncertainty sets and exact conformal differentiation—remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation through explanations of why smaller uncertainty sets need not yield better decisions, why optimization dominates training cost, and how differing solvers complicate timing comparisons. It also discusses poor local optima motivating pretraining and identifies conditional calibration as a remaining challenge. Existing distribution-shift and nonconvexity limitations largely persist.

D1.justification: v2 supplies previously omitted Gaussian-mixture means, exact temporal split dates, and timing-specific hardware and Clarabel/SCS solver details. It also revises documented PICNN hyperparameters. Both versions already provide the same code repository and most architecture, optimizer and data-processing information.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning against decision-aware conformal classification and surrogate decision-focused learning, adding discussions of Kiyani, Cortes-Gomez, Elmachtoub–Grigas, Wilder and Mandi. It substantially revises its comparison with Chenreddy–Delage and Wang, including reasons for excluding the former from experiments and acknowledgment of the latter's updated conditional formulation.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work comparison, method exposition and conclusion receive extensive rewriting. Sections 3.1 and 3.2 exchange order, experimental results become the first appendix, and the remaining appendices are reorganized. The separate limitations discussion is largely integrated into future-work prose.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to contrast ETO and E2E workflows. Battery plots are merged into paired shift/no-shift displays, and portfolio plots become Tables A2–A3. v2 adds Figure 2, Figures A1–A4 and runtime Table A1, alongside substantial journal-style typography and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new tail-risk tests and runtime disclosures make robustness and computational claims more assessable, while missing data-generation details and clearer visual organization improve reproducibility and understanding. These provide a net benefit, limited by the inconsistent box-score rewrite in Section 3.1 and removal of the portfolio oracle reference.
